prerequisites: Knowledge of protocol architectures and the lower layers (physical and data link) of the OSI model, as covered in the 'Fundamentos de Telemática' course.
Proficiency in binary, decimal, and hexadecimal numerical representations.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, enabling the learning of new methods and technologies, and providing great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Telecommunication Technical Engineer's activity.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, task planning, and other similar works in their specific field of telecommunication.
Facility for handling specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

Ability to work in a multidisciplinary group and in a multilingual environment and to communicate, both in writing and orally, knowledge, procedures, results, and ideas related to telecommunications and electronics.

Ability to use communication and computer applications (office automation, databases, advanced calculation, project management, visualization, etc.) to support the development and operation of telecommunication and electronic networks, services, and applications.
Ability to use computer tools for searching bibliographic resources or information related to telecommunications and electronics.

Ability to conceive, deploy, organize and manage telecommunication networks, systems, services, and infrastructures in residential (home, city, and digital communities), business, or institutional contexts, taking responsibility for their implementation and continuous improvement, as well as knowing their economic and social impact.
Knowledge and use of network architecture, protocols, and communication interface concepts.
Knowledge of network interconnection and routing methods, as well as the fundamentals of network planning and sizing based on traffic parameters.
Recognize topologies in local area networks, name the protocols that could be used, and explain their operation.
Analyze, elaborate, and determine relevant information in the development of works related to the different topics that will be addressed in the subject.
Know the methods of routing and network interconnection.
Analyze and evaluate routing protocols using computer tools.
Create and use models of real networks using network simulators.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: Review of Physical and Data Link Layers
Routing: Classification, strategies, and minimum cost algorithms
Introduction to congestion control and traffic management techniques
Interior routing protocols: RIP, introduction to OSPF
Exterior routing protocols: Introduction to BGP

assessment_methods.method: Theory evaluation (Nt) - Ordinary call: Controls during classroom practices or global theory exam
Practice evaluation (Np) - Ordinary call: Activities during the semester (Nap) and final practice exam (Nep)
Theory evaluation (Nt) - Other calls: Theory exam
Practice evaluation (Np) - Other calls: Practice exam

assessment_rules: To pass the course, both the theory (Nt) and practical (Np) blocks must be passed with a minimum of 5 out of 10 points. If this condition is not met, the maximum final grade will be 4.5 points. If both blocks are passed, the final grade is calculated as 0.6 * Nt + 0.4 * Np. Grades for passed blocks are carried over between calls within the same academic year. For the ordinary call, theory is assessed through controls (average if each is >= 4, else max 4.5 for theory; if global theory < 5, a global exam is required); practices require 80% attendance and Np = 0.1 * Nap + 0.9 * Nep. For other calls, both Nt and Np are determined by their respective exams.
